headline: Agents, Automations, and Design Systems
subheadline: Figma's May release notes drop with AI agent co-design, Cursor ships cloud agent environments, and there's a meaty deep-dive on agentic design systems that's directly relevant to your MCP + white-label work.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma's May 2026 Release Notes — AI Agent Co-Design is Here
sections.description: Figma's May release notes just dropped and the headline feature is learning to co-design with AI agents. Given that you're literally building a Figma MCP + Claude integration for your company's design system, this could either validate your approach or change it. Worth watching the live demos closely — they're showing real workflows from product teams.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma AI in 2026: Everything It Can Do — and What It Still Can't
sections.description: An honest breakdown of where Figma AI actually delivers versus where it's still falling short. As someone operating at expert level, you'll appreciate the candor — it separates the real capabilities (content generation, prototype population) from the marketing fluff. Useful for calibrating expectations on your own MCP integration work.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Cursor Ships Cloud Agent Development Environments
sections.description: Cursor's latest release (May 20) introduces cloud agent dev environments and improved Automations — parallel agents running end to end. Since you're vibe-coding with Cursor daily, this is a meaningful workflow upgrade. Cloud environments mean you can kick off agents and not block your local machine. Check the changelog for the specifics.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: The Future of Enterprise Design Systems: Agentic AI in 2026
sections.description: This is the one to bookmark. Supernova lays out a practical roadmap for design systems in the age of agentic AI — automating token management, scaling component libraries, future-proofing workflows. It speaks directly to what you're building: a design system that AI agents can actually work with. The enterprise framing also maps well to white-label architecture.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Design Patterns for AI Agents
sections.description: A community discussion on the emerging design patterns that will define AI agents in 2026. You mentioned being early on AI agents but curious — this thread breaks down patterns like tool-use orchestration, memory architectures, and human-in-the-loop flows. Good foundational vocabulary for someone building agent-connected design tools.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Every New Claude Code Feature Explained (May 2026)
sections.description: Anthropic shipped a massive wave of Claude Code updates this month — voice input, desktop computer use, and more. You're already deep in Claude Code, so this is less tutorial and more 'here's what's new that you might have missed.' The voice input alone could change how you work during maternity leave.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Lovable Mobile App — Vibe-Code from Your Phone
sections.description: Lovable just shipped iOS and Android apps. You already use Lovable on desktop, but a mobile app means you could prototype or iterate on ideas from the couch or during nap time. It's being pitched as a way to go from idea to working app entirely from your phone. Worth downloading to see if the mobile experience holds up.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If AI agents can co-design in Figma, what does your MCP integration become?
sections.description: Figma is officially building AI agent co-design into the platform. You're building a custom MCP + Claude integration for your company's design system. The question isn't whether these will compete — it's whether Figma's native agent features make your custom integration more powerful (by handling the basics) or less necessary. Worth thinking through your differentiation layer.
